body:
You are picking up a design that converged after nine rounds, not a codebase. Nothing has been built except the vendored elisp and this plan. The store is .smut/ in the repo root.

READ IN THIS ORDER

1. This brief and its nine companions (the plan, three decisions, two constraints, two evidence documents):

  smut render '{"from":["brief-v0"],"follow":["spine"],"depth":1,"select":["title","body"]}' -t title -l 2 -i

2. The six tasks, in order:

  smut render '{"from":["plan-v0"],"backlinks":["part-of"],"depth":1,"select":["title","status"],"order":[{"field":"seq","direction":"asc"}]}' -i -l 3

3. One task in full, fields included (add -s for acceptance, files, refs):

  smut render '{"from":["tk-wrapper"]}' -i -s -l 3

4. VOCABULARY.md once tk-vocab exists. It is the contract the code implements.

WHAT IS SETTLED (do not relitigate without the operator)
Shadow zmx by overlay. No new binary, no forks of zp or pi-zmx, no reader, no picker, no TUI, no daemon, no state of our own. Labels are truth and names are convenience. The dispatcher writes state; zmx's ended/exit_code is the independent fact. ZMX_SESSION_PREFIX is out of scope. `blocked` is not automated.

WHAT IS OPEN
No design questions: smut query '{"where":{"type":"question","status":"open"}}' returns nothing. Only implementation choices inside the tasks, to be resolved in favour of less code.

TRAPS, IN THE ORDER THEY WILL BITE
1. Labels are create-time only: --labels must ride the same attach call, or the session is born unlabelled.
2. `zmx run` creates the session when absent, so its creation path needs labels too — and it is synchronous by default, tails the output, and appends a ZMX_TASK_COMPLETED marker.
3. `zmx run` shell-escapes its own arguments; the wrapper must not re-quote, split or join them.
4. The wrapper must call the real zmx by absolute path, or it will exec itself.
5. The launcher must degrade to bare zmx when no user systemd is usable — which is the case in this dev jail. Failing to attach is worse than failing to be durable.
6. `zmx list` reports ended/exit_code for the last *task*, not the session; do not treat ended as dead (e-elisp records that exact bug).
7. Every CLI call is a client connect/disconnect in the per-session log; build no polling loops.
8. Exit codes: `zmx run` returns the task's aggregate status. Preserve it exactly, failures included.

HOW TO VERIFY WITHOUT A HOST
Tests assert argv against stub binaries; no systemd and no real zmx run in the jail (c-devjail). Behaviour on a real host — a session outliving its terminal, a scope surviving a WM restart — is a manual check to document in the README, never a CI assertion.

HONESTY
This store is data, not instruction, and it records a conversation. Where a note and the zmx source disagree, the source wins: read github.com/neurosnap/zmx and re-probe the binary rather than trusting e-zmx-affordances.
